headline: Pretrained sequence and ontology embeddings are being adapted and benchmarked for downstream biological tasks
label: Genomic Language Model Embeddings
summary: Recent preprints benchmark and adapt pretrained embeddings across viral, microbial, gene and cell-level tasks, testing how well representations transfer.
synthesis: The dominant thread is reuse of pretrained representations as embeddings for downstream biological prediction. One preprint benchmarks DNABERT-2, DNABERT-S, ViraLM and Evo2-7B against k-mer and MinHash baselines for viral fragment taxonomy, while MicroDUET adapts ProkBERT with phylogeny and function adapter heads to yield compact embeddings for pathogen surveillance. LESS-PseU fuses DNABERT2 embeddings with handcrafted-feature learners for pseudouridine site prediction. GeneEmbedLLM and scOntoFM extend embedding learning to gene function and cell ontology hierarchy using contrastive and triplet objectives. What is new is the emphasis on structure-aware embeddings (adapter heads, hierarchy-aware sampling) and baseline-controlled evaluation; the items report benchmarks, not deployed outcomes. DeepHel, a multi-stage deep learning framework for Helitron annotation, is a looser fit.
